name: Jaipur
short: Palaces, forts, old-city lanes and craft markets.
about: Jaipur works well for a short cultural trip. Spend your mornings around major forts and palaces, keep the afternoons for museums and old-city lanes, and leave an evening for local food and markets.
tip: Give yourself at least one full day inside the forts before rushing on to the next city — Jaipur rewards travellers who slow down.

name: Goa
short: Beaches, Portuguese-era streets, seafood and relaxed evenings.
about: Goa can be planned around either busy beach areas or quieter southern stretches. A good plan balances beach time with Panjim and heritage stops.
tip: North Goa gets busy in peak season, so if you want quiet beaches, plan a couple of days further south.

name: Manali
short: Mountain roads, river valleys, cafés and high-altitude scenery.
about: Manali is best enjoyed without overpacking the itinerary. Keep a full day for the valley and local areas, then use remaining days for scenic excursions and flexible outdoor time.
tip: Roads to the higher valleys can close briefly after fresh snow, so keep a spare day in hand during winter.

name: Kerala
short: Backwaters, tropical landscapes, houseboats and slow travel.
about: Kerala suits travellers who want several landscape types in one trip. Combine a hill stop with a backwater stay and a city or heritage segment.
tip: Book houseboats a few weeks ahead in peak season (November to February) — the good ones fill up fast.

name: Kashmir
short: Lakes, meadows, mountain views and scenic valley stays.
about: Kashmir trips are strongest when the itinerary leaves room for scenery rather than only ticking attractions off a list. Choose one base for a relaxed pace and day trips around it.
tip: Pahalgam and Gulmarg are each worth a full day trip from Srinagar rather than a rushed half-day stop.

name: Rajasthan
short: Fort cities, royal architecture, desert landscapes and local food.
about: Rajasthan works especially well as a multi-city road itinerary. Keep transfer days realistic, then leave enough time in each city to explore beyond one landmark.
tip: Trains and cabs between cities take longer than they look on a map — build in real travel time, not just distance.

name: Agra
short: A focused heritage stop around one of India’s best-known monuments.
about: Agra can be handled as a compact stop with one full day. Start early for the Taj Mahal and keep the rest of the day for nearby heritage sights.
tip: Arrive at the Taj Mahal at sunrise; it's far quieter and the light is better than any other time of day.

name: Udaipur
short: Lakeside views, palaces and slower evenings in the old city.
about: Udaipur is suited to a slower two- or three-day break. Mix palace visits with time near the lakes and old-city streets.
tip: Book a lake-facing table for dinner at least a day ahead — the good spots overlooking Lake Pichola fill up quickly.
